<warning>Xylograph printed in red ink in Manchu script, with a Chinese label in the right-hand frame panel. The Manchu body text and the small Manchu label in the left-hand frame panel are not transcribed, because a romanization could not be produced reliably from this image. The paper is stained and creased, and the ink is pale in places.</warning>
<meta>Pothi-format leaf inside a double-ruled frame with a scrolling floral border. Narrow labelled panels at the left and right ends, each with cloud-scroll corner ornaments. Running Manchu text in vertical columns, read left to right. The left label panel and the first body column end with punctuation marks.</meta>

<image-desc size="large" type="decorative" significance="low">Printed red frame around the whole text block. A double rule encloses a band of continuous scrolling foliate ornament. At each end a narrow vertical panel is set off by rules and decorated with cloud-scroll (ruyi) corner motifs; these panels hold the volume and folio labels.</image-desc>

translation.text:
<meta>Source language is Manchu, not Mongolian as specified in the request. The Manchu body text and the left-hand Manchu label were not transcribed in the OCR, so only the frame description and the Chinese marginal label can be translated. No continuity with a previous page can be established.</meta>

<warning>The OCR did not transcribe the main Manchu text of this page. It is kept as unread material below, and no translation is supplied for it.</warning>

<note>A red printed frame surrounds the whole text block. A double rule encloses a band of continuous scrolling leaf ornament. At each end, a narrow vertical panel is marked off by rules and decorated at its corners with cloud-scroll motifs, known as ruyi. These panels hold the volume and folio labels.</note>

<margin><unclear>Manchu marginal label in the left-hand panel, 4–5 words (title and folio reference), not transcribed</unclear></margin>

<unclear>About 20 vertical columns of printed Manchu text (sutra text), not transcribed</unclear>

<margin>Great Jewel-Heap Sutra, Volume Two, Part One, folio 2 <note>original: "大寶積經第二卷上二". This is the Chinese title of the <term>Ratnakūṭa Sūtra</term> <gloss>Heap of Jewels discourse</gloss>, a large Mahāyāna collection of 49 separate sutras. The final character 二 gives the folio number.</note></margin>

<summary>This is folio 2 of Volume Two, Part One, of the Great Jewel-Heap Sutra (Ratnakūṭa), from a Manchu xylograph printed in red ink. The Manchu sutra text was not transcribed, so only the Chinese folio label and the decorative frame can be rendered.</summary>
